To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the use of statistical methods for knowledge extraction from text is effective; (b) probabilistic reasoning over extracted knowledge can be performed in a scalable way; and (c) human feedback can be used to reduce uncertainty resulting from both knowledge extraction and probabilistic inference

(1) the MADDEN system can extract a high percentage of the facts contained in a given text corpus; (2) the PROBKB system can derive additional facts not present in the text corpus; (3) the CAMEL system can reduce uncertainty by using human input to correct errors in the extraction and deduction processes; (4) the overall system is able to produce a knowledge base containing a large percentage of the relevant facts contained in the text corpus

(1) MADDEN is capable of extracting knowledge from a large number of text sources, including the Web, and that (2) PROBKB and CAMEL are effective in improving the quality of the knowledge extracted by MADDEN.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three problems: (1) how to construct a probabilistic knowledge base from unstructured text, (2) how to perform probabilistic reasoning over such a knowledge base, and (3) how to leverage human feedback to improve the quality of the constructed knowledge base.

the following three questions: (1) What is the most effective way of extracting information from text? (2) How can we use extracted facts to derive additional facts? (3) How can we combine machine and human intelligence to build a robust knowledge base?
